messages.content:
Jessica the jackrabbit wants to climb down a wall. The wall consists of 2026 horizontal layers stacked vertically. The $n$th layer from the top is partitioned into $2^n - 1$ identical rectangular bricks arranged side by side. Jessica begins in the topmost layer, which contains a single brick. A move consists of Jessica going down one layer to a brick that shares a side with the brick she is currently on.

Determine, with proof, the total number of distinct sequences of moves Jessica can take to reach the 2026th layer.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
We interpret “shares a side” in the usual full-side sense: a lower brick must have its entire top side in contact with the brick above it. A brick whose top side is split between two upper bricks does not share a full side with either.

Scale the wall so its total width is \(1\).  
In layer \(n\), there are

\[
m_n=2^n-1
\]

bricks, so the \(i\)-th brick of layer \(n\) has horizontal interval

\[
\left[\frac{i-1}{m_n},\frac{i}{m_n}\right].
\]

For \(n\ge 2\), write \(m=m_n\). Then layer \(n+1\) has \(2m+1\) bricks. In units of the width of a brick in layer \(n+1\), the \(i\)-th brick of layer \(n\) spans

\[
\left[2(i-1)+\frac{i-1}{m},\; 2i+\frac{i}{m}\right].
\]

A brick \(j\) in layer \(n+1\) spans \([j-1,j]\) in these units. It is wholly beneath brick \(i\) of layer \(n\) exactly when

\[
j-1\ge 2(i-1)+\frac{i-1}{m}
\quad\text{and}\quad
j\le 2i+\frac{i}{m}.
\]

Checking the three possible positions of brick \(i\):

- If \(i=1\), then \(j=1,2\) work.
- If \(1<i<m\), then the only possibility is \(j=2i\).
- If \(i=m\), then \(j=2m,2m+1\) work.

Thus, for every layer \(n\ge 2\):

- the leftmost and rightmost bricks each have \(2\) bricks below sharing a full side;
- every interior brick has exactly \(1\) such brick below.

For the top layer, the single brick has all \(3\) bricks of layer \(2\) below it.

Now let \(R_n\) be the number of reachable bricks in layer \(n\). The leftmost and rightmost bricks are reachable in every layer, because each leftmost brick lies wholly beneath the previous leftmost brick, and similarly on the right.

Also, a lower brick can be wholly beneath at most one brick in the layer above, so no reachable brick has two different parents. Therefore each reachable brick gives exactly one distinct sequence of moves to itself.

For \(n\ge 2\), every reachable brick contributes one reachable brick below it, and the two reachable end bricks contribute one extra each. Hence

\[
R_{n+1}=R_n+2.
\]

We have \(R_1=1\) and \(R_2=3\), so by induction

\[
R_n=2n-1.
\]

Thus the number of distinct sequences of moves to reach layer \(2026\) is

\[
R_{2026}=2(2026)-1=4051.
\]

\[
\boxed{4051}
\]
